answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits show fabricated results. A sybil attacker must lock real capital for every persona, so multiplying identities raises the cost rather than creating free influence; coordinated fraud also risks losing the whole stake. Set the bond carefully: at the nadir of honest agents’ cash flow, an excessive bond could trigger a spiral that excludes them, leaving the mechanism a relic rather than a defense.
